summary: This Dockerfile builds a development container based on a production image. It installs essential Linux tools, creates a non-root user for development, configures the bash shell with history and a custom prompt, sets up VS Code server folders, changes ownership of the app directory to the new user, and installs Python dependencies.

explanations.5: ARG defines a build-time variable that can be passed when building the image; here it sets the numeric user ID for the new user account.
explanations.12: ENV sets environment variables that persist in the running container; these two tell Python not to cache bytecode and to output logs immediately without buffering.
explanations.19: RUN --mount=type=cache caches the apt package lists between builds so Docker doesn't re-download everything each time you rebuild.
explanations.20: set -eux makes the shell script strict: exit on errors, print commands before running, and treat undefined variables as errors.
explanations.39: This checks if a user with the given name already exists; if not, it creates the user and group in the lines that follow.
explanations.46: This comment explains why we need these VS Code server folders owned by the non-root user instead of root.
explanations.56: This appends configuration to the user's .bashrc file (which runs every time they open a new shell) to set where bash history is saved.
explanations.68: MARKER is a comment string we use as a sentinel; we check if it's already in the file so we don't add the welcome message twice.
explanations.69: The grep -qxF checks quietly if that exact marker line exists; if not (||), we append the welcome message using a here-document (the cat <<EOF syntax).
explanations.83: chown changes file ownership; here we make sure the app directory is owned by the non-root user instead of root, so they can edit code.
explanations.85: USER switches from running commands as root to running them as the non-root user for the rest of the build and when the container starts.
explanations.89: Like line 19, this caches pip's downloaded packages between rebuilds to speed things up.
